core.title: Preserve the real proof boundary in SMOKE tests
core.given: A test file whose declared Phase is SMOKE
core.when: the tester writes or edits a case in that file
core.then: Preserve the real proof boundary: the case MUST exercise the production collaborator through the assembled path the SMOKE acceptance requires, on the real infrastructure or environment the declared smoke proof verifies, and MUST NOT substitute any production collaborator.
prefer: Arrange only the minimum preconditions needed for the declared stimulus.
Observe the acceptance-specific external result after the real collaborator runs.
If substitution is the intended proof technique, move the case into a UNIT-phase test where it is honest and expected.
avoid: Replacing the collaborator the SMOKE claim depends on because it is expensive, inconvenient or hard to arrange — that changes the question, not the cost.
Moving the test inward to a unit seam merely because it is easier to control.
Relabeling a case as SMOKE after substituting collaborators in ways that bypass production behavior.
unless: The file is not SMOKE-phase: UNIT tests may substitute freely.
core.why: In a SMOKE proof the boundary is part of the claim: a substituted SMOKE test (perhaps a fine unit test) earns the gate credit that the real path works when the real path is precisely what was replaced, letting a green suite coexist with a broken deployment — the failure the phase separation between UNIT and SMOKE exists to prevent.
evidence: The stack's tester-discipline check reports no substitution call in any SMOKE-phase file, each finding reported at an exact location.
The case would fail if the real collaborator or production wiring were broken.
The observable assertion proves the bound acceptance rather than the test fixture.
verification: Scope: only files whose declared Phase is SMOKE are scanned; files of other phases (e.g. UNIT) are not scanned and may substitute freely.

The check flags any substitution call on a production collaborator in a SMOKE-phase file, reporting an exact location for each finding; which constructs count as substitution is stack data taken from the profile.
A substitution finding is violation evidence, not an activation prerequisite: the rule also fires when the tester creates or edits any case in a SMOKE-phase file, including a currently compliant one.
Reading the declared Phase requires a phase observer that parses the file's own Phase declaration; no filename or location convention is assumed.
Severity 4; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

Not covered by the scan: the behavioral evidence — that the case would fail if the real collaborator or production wiring were broken, and that the observable assertion proves the bound acceptance rather than the test fixture — is not established by this substitution scan alone; the rule does not prescribe the means by which it is established.

fires: The tester creates or edits any case in a test file declaring Phase SMOKE, including a currently compliant one.
A SMOKE-phase test substitutes a production collaborator using the stack's substitution constructs.
A test that substitutes collaborators is being relabeled as SMOKE.
doesNotFire: A UNIT-phase test file substitutes collaborators.
Non-test source files with no declared test Phase.

neutralityNotes: ATDD-level vocabulary — Phase names (SMOKE, UNIT), 'gate', 'acceptance', 'assembled path' — is kept in the core because it is method, not stack. The Bun rule's activation.fires[1] and doesNotFire[0] name concrete APIs; the core's fires/doesNotFire say 'substitutes collaborators', instantiated per stack by idiom.test_constructs#collaborator_substitution. Test-file language scoping is realized through the proposed tooling.language_scopes#test_languages key, not through tooling.languages, whose vocabulary meaning (production-source languages) is preserved. The smoke-acceptance URN shape and binding syntax, if a realization needs them, belong to the existing urn.* keys, but bun.json states neither, so no bunValue can be given for them here. Severity 4 and the strict disposition are kept as declared, in core:verification, not as profile keys. The behavioral evidence (counterfactual failure, acceptance-specific assertion) is retained verbatim in core:evidence; the verification entry only excludes the substitution scan from establishing it and prescribes no means of establishing it.
